summary: 书评介绍阿普顿如何从住宅、社区、自然、技术与艺术理解美国建筑。评论者肯定其广度，也指出书中忽略了家庭农庄。

sentences: by Dell Upton
戴尔·厄普顿著。
paragraphs.gist: 《美国建筑》的作者是戴尔·厄普顿。

paragraphs.brief: 五个主题串起建筑与社会史
sentences: As its title suggests, Architecture in the United States is an ambitious work, and there are few scholars as qualified to undertake such a project as Dell Upton, a distinguished scholar of American architectural history who, having a background in American studies, is as knowledgeable in vernacular architecture as high style.
正如其标题所示，美国建筑是一项雄心勃勃的工作，很少有学者有资格开展这样一个项目，例如Dell Upton，他是一位美国建筑史的杰出学者，具有美国研究背景，对本地建筑有如高风格般的了解。
The book is structured into five themes: Community, Nature, Technology, Money, and Art.
该书分为五个主题：社区、自然、技术、金钱和艺术。

The usefulness of this technique becomes apparent as one progresses through the book and realizes that Upton discusses not only houses and farm and commercial buildings but also landscape architecture, gardens, bridges, public sculpture, and whole cities.
这一技术的有用性随着书本的进步而变得显而易见，并意识到乌普顿不仅讨论房屋、农场和商业建筑，而且讨论景观建筑、花园、桥梁、公共雕塑和整个城市。
His thematic structure is also well coordinated with his intention to examine architecture not primarily as a form of art but as an integral part of social and economic history.
按主题组织全书，也符合厄普顿的写作意图：把建筑当作社会经济史不可分割的一部分来考察，不仅着眼于它的艺术形式。
paragraphs.gist: 厄普顿用社区、自然、技术、金钱和艺术五个主题串联美国建筑，把建筑形式放回社会与经济史中考察。

paragraphs.brief: 从住宅理解家庭与社会
sentences: The first chapter, “An American Icon,” is devoted to the house.
第一章题为“美国的象征”，专门讨论住宅。

Upton’s discussion of this elemental unit of architecture and its importance per the primary social structure of the family is an effective introduction to the broad topic of architecture in relationship to society.
住宅是建筑的基本单元，也与家庭这一基本社会结构密切相关，厄普顿从这里切入，自然引出了建筑与社会的广泛联系。
While much of the chapter focuses on examples of elite houses, in particular Thomas Jefferson’s Monticello, Upton incorporates much essential information about folk houses into his interpretations.
虽然该章大部分侧重于精英住房的例子，特别是托马斯·杰斐逊的Monticello，但乌普顿将关于民宅的许多基本信息纳入了他的解释。

This chapter, like the succeeding five, follows a loose chronological orientation in its analysis of several examples of homes from the seventeenth to twentieth centuries, while integrating discussion of form and style with social and economic processes.
与后续五章一样，本章大致按时间顺序分析了 17 至 20 世纪的若干住宅，将建筑形式与风格同社会、经济变迁联系起来。
paragraphs.gist: 首章从家庭居住空间切入，以杰斐逊的蒙蒂塞洛庄园等宅邸和民居为例，串起几个世纪里住宅形制与社会经济生活的变化。

paragraphs.brief: 社区和自然怎样塑造建筑
sentences: Chapter 2, “Community,” examines monumental architecture ranging from Native American earthworks and courthouse square models to state and federal capitols, memorials, and other public buildings, connecting them to issues such as the metaphor of the ancestral homeland, the Colonial Revival, planned communities, and other architectural definitions of community.
第二章“社区”从美洲原住民的土方建筑、法院广场的布局写到州及联邦议会大厦、纪念建筑和其他公共建筑，讨论祖居地的象征、殖民复兴风格和规划社区等如何通过建筑表达共同体观念。
In chapter 3, “Nature,” Upton posits a theological role for nature with respect to American architecture because of the enormous influence of the wilderness on the identity of the country.
在第三章“自然”中，厄普顿认为，由于荒野对国家特征的巨大影响，自然在神学上对美国建筑具有作用。
From first settlement onwards, architecture “was an ally against nature” (p. 107).
从移民初次定居起，建筑就是他们“对抗自然的盟友”（第 107 页）。
He contrasts this attitude, and its reflection in architecture, with that of Native Americans and their built environment.
他将这种态度及其在建筑中的反映与美洲原住民及其建筑环境的对比。

By the nineteenth century, the dynamic relationship between nature and culture was expressed in the creation of urban parks, suburban homes and movements such as the Picturesque, Primitivism, and Arts and Crafts, whose most notable product was the ubiquitous bungalow.
到了 19 世纪，自然与文化的互动体现在城市公园和郊区住宅，也体现在如画美学、原始主义和工艺美术运动中，其中最显眼的产物便是随处可见的平房。
paragraphs.gist: 社区篇用土方建筑、法院广场和议会大厦解读群体认同，自然篇则比较移民与原住民对荒野的态度，并追溯这些观念如何塑造城市公园和郊区住宅。

sentences: Chapter 4, “Technology,” begins with a description of traditional timber framing and its evolution in the nineteenth century into balloon framing and prefabrication.
第四章“技术”先介绍传统木框架，以及这种结构在 19 世纪怎样发展为贯通立柱式轻木框架和预制建筑。
Upton neglects those muddy realms of interest to the folk architecture scholar, such as why many farmers still built heavy, timber-frame, pegged barns well into the twentieth century.
厄普顿略过了民间建筑学者关心的一些棘手问题，例如为何进入 20 世纪后，许多农民仍用木销连接的粗木框架搭建谷仓。
He moves quickly to discussion of industrial buildings and bridges, connecting Americans’ fascination with technology to the aesthetic category of the Sublime.
他很快转向工业建筑和桥梁，将美国人对技术的迷恋与美学中的“崇高”概念联系起来。
Finally, Upton analyzes Utopianism and Consumerism in architecture and their connection to industrial design and notable architects such as Buckminster Fuller.
最后，乌普顿分析了建筑中的乌托邦主义和消费主义及其与工业设计和诸如巴克明斯特·富勒等著名建筑师的联系。

Chapter 5, “Money,” segues naturally from the previous chapter: after an elaborate discussion of Pueblo Indian towns and their relationship to their society and economy, Upton describes the growth of major American cities and the role of commerce in that growth.
第五章“金钱”自然承接前章，先详述普韦布洛人的城镇与当地社会经济的关系，再介绍美国大城市的兴起和商业在其中的作用。
This “cultural construction of economic life” (p. 207) culminated in the skyscraper and is intricately connected to what Upton calls “the moral authority of Capitalism” (p. 223).
这种“经济生活文化建设”(第207页)最终形成摩天大楼，与乌普顿所谓的“资本主义道德权威”(第223页)有着错综复杂的联系。
From there he moves to an architectural interpretation of shopping malls and markets.
他从那里走向对购物中心和市场的建筑解释。
paragraphs.gist: 技术篇把木构、桥梁和工业设计联系到美国人对技术的迷恋，金钱篇则从普韦布洛城镇写到商业城市、摩天大楼和购物空间。

paragraphs.brief: 建筑师职业与风格的形成
sentences: The concluding chapter, “Art,” begins by examining the historical conception of architecture.
最后一章“艺术”首先审查建筑的历史概念。
American architecture as a profession began in the nineteenth century and, as the century progressed, the architect’s role became increasingly divorced from that of the builder.
美国建筑师这一专业在 19 世纪形成，随着时间推移，建筑师与营造者的职责越来越分明。
Upton connects this progression to “the growing separation of head-work from handwork in all segments of the American economy” (p. 254).
厄普顿把这一变化与“美国经济各领域脑力与体力劳动日益分离”联系起来（第 254 页）。

However, architecture as a profession had inherited a special status, like art, from its role as a vehicle of social identity: “Architects claimed superiority to builders based on their taste, cultivated through special training, socialization, and immersion in architecture. …
然而，建筑作为职业，从它作为社会认同工具的作用中继承了与艺术一样的特殊地位：" 建筑师根据他们的品味向建筑商主张优势，这种优势是通过特殊培训、社会化和建筑业沉浸而培养的……
The new architects were manufactured gentlemen who in turn sold their tastes in a consumer economy” (p. 255).
新的建筑师是制造出来的绅士，他们转而销售他们在消费经济中的品味”(第255页)。
The folklorist will recognize here many of the attributes used to distinguish elite culture from popular or folk culture.
研究民俗的人会在这里认出许多常被用来区分精英文化与大众或民间文化的特征。

Upton continues with a discussion of the concept of “style” and its importance to the field of architecture: style is basically a visual vocabulary used to denote what is fashionable and was useful for claiming social place as well as contributing to professional standardization.
Upton继续讨论“风格”的概念及其对建筑领域的重要性：风格基本上是一种直观词汇，用来表示什么是时尚的，对于主张社会地位和推动专业标准化是有用的。

Upton ends the chapter with the significant subtitle “Beyond Art”: “Every architect and every building belongs to several overlapping ‘high’ and ‘vernacular’ circles of architectural knowledge,” he says.
厄普顿以“超越艺术”收束本章，指出每位建筑师和每座建筑都同时属于若干相互重叠的“精英”与“乡土”建筑知识圈。
“These circles of architectural knowledge encompass technologies, social ideas, and meanings that are unaccounted for in, and often antagonistic to, art-architectural traditions” (p. 189).
“这些建筑知识圈涵盖的技术、社会观念及其意义，常常超出艺术建筑传统所能解释的范围，甚至与之抵触”（第 189 页）。
paragraphs.gist: 末章追溯建筑师如何从营造者中分化为专业群体，并指出建筑风格虽能彰显身份，技术和社会观念也塑造了超出艺术传统的建筑知识。

paragraphs.brief: 评论者如何看待乡土建筑
sentences: My only complaint about this masterful work is that it neglects one facet of American architecture that is essentially connected to American history, society, and economy, and that is the farmstead.
我唯一抱怨的就是，它忽略了美国建筑的一个方面，基本上与美国的历史、社会和经济有关，也就是农场。

The vast majority of built structures in this country until the twentieth century were of folk architectural origins, but the importance of the family farmstead to the construction of American society is often neglected nowadays.
直到20世纪，这个国家绝大多数建筑结构都是民间建筑，但家庭农场对建设美国社会的重要性现在常常被忽视。

Architecture in the United States has a bias toward the urban and elite over the rural or folk in terms of its coverage, but the fact that it knowledgeably includes any discussion of folk architecture at all is a testament to the tremendous progress that field has made in the past thirty years.
《美国建筑》的篇幅偏重城市与精英建筑，但作者能以专业眼光讨论民间建筑，本身已见证这一领域过去三十年的长足进步。
In this beautifully written and illustrated book, Upton displays his commanding expertise in all areas of architecture.
这本书文字优美、插图出色，也充分显示了厄普顿在各类建筑问题上的深厚造诣。
paragraphs.gist: 评论者惋惜书中忽略家庭农庄、偏重城市和精英建筑，同时肯定作者对民间建筑的重视及全书贯通各领域的功力。
